title: 3.4.21 Lab: Parameters, Return Values, and Arrow Syntax
description: Write a function with a parameter and a return value, a second function of your own, and an arrow function, then call them and print the results. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Declare a function
steps.instructions: Create a function called `greet` that takes a name parameter and returns a greeting string.

steps.title: Write a second function
steps.instructions: Write a second function of your own, with at least one parameter, that returns a value built from its parameter.

steps.title: Write an arrow function
steps.instructions: Write an arrow function using the short form from the reading: a const, the parameters, =>, then the expression.

steps.title: Call your functions and print
steps.instructions: Call greet with a name and print what it hands back with console.log. Call the other two as well and print their results.

requirements.title: greet function
requirements.description: Declare a function called greet. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: A function declaration starts with the word function, then the name greet, then parentheses and a body in braces.

requirements.title: Return value
requirements.description: Return a value: a return statement, or an arrow whose body is one expression
requirements.hint: A function can hand a value back. Use the return keyword followed by the value you want to give back.

requirements.title: Arrow function
requirements.description: Write an arrow function. Help: 3.4.6 (Arrow Functions)
requirements.hint: An arrow function is written with =>. Put the parameters before the arrow and the body after it.

requirements.title: Call greet
requirements.description: Call the greet function. Help: 3.1.11 (The Function-Call Shape)
requirements.hint: Defining a function does nothing until you call it. Write its name followed by parentheses.

requirements.title: Multiple functions
requirements.description: Define at least 2 functions. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: Write two separate function definitions, not one. Give each its own name and body.

requirements.title: greet returns a greeting with the name
requirements.description: greet("Ava") returns a greeting that contains Ava, and the same works for another name. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: greet must hand back a string built from its parameter: return "Hello, " + name + "!". Printing inside greet is not the same as returning.

requirements.title: Results printed
requirements.description: Print what your functions return with console.log. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: Wrap each call in console.log so you can see what it hands back: console.log(greet("Ava")).
